title: Airline held liable for its chatbot's invented refund policy
blast_radius: One customer, CAD $812.02 in damages and fees. The precedent is the larger blast radius: a tribunal held that a company is responsible for what its chatbot says.
summary: A customer asked the airline's website chatbot about bereavement fares and was told a discount could be claimed retroactively after travel. The airline's actual published policy required the request before the flight. When the refund was refused, the customer took the case to a civil resolution tribunal, which found negligent misrepresentation and ordered the airline to pay. The tribunal rejected the argument that the chatbot was a separate entity, holding that a chatbot is part of the company's website like any other page.
containment: Damages awarded to the customer; the chatbot was subsequently withdrawn from the site.
